title: Scrub the shipped client name and define Pipeman's publish step

history.detail:
PASS: PASS — round 1. Audited 976f3d2 (release content) on top of e2014ff (bookkeeping). Sprint file read fresh immediately before this verdict.

Precondition checked before auditing anything: sprint 4's Dependencies block says it must not start until sprint 3 is closed and 0.1.3 actually published. Sprint 3's state file reads phase complete, groundtruth_result PASS, live_test_rounds 1, and LiveQA's recorded notes say the test ran against the real registry. Precondition genuinely satisfied, not assumed.

REQUIREMENTS COVERAGE

Req 1 — MET in the file that matters. scripts/launcher/session.js no longer contains the client project name or the machine-specific directory count. See CRITERION SCOPE below for the grep.

Req 1a — MET, and this is the requirement that could most easily have been botched. Read the before and after side by side at 89c8a74 vs 976f3d2. All three named elements survive verbatim:
  - empirical derivation: "verified by hand against real macOS session directories while building this"
  - re-verification across character classes: "Re-verified against a path containing a space, two consecutive spaces, a dot, parentheses, and single/double underscores"
  - Windows flagged as extrapolation: "is the reasonable extrapolation, but Windows itself remains unverified"
Also preserved: the admission that an earlier version of the function assumed slashes only and was failed on it. That is the part of the comment that makes the rest trustworthy, and it would have been the easiest line to quietly drop while scrubbing. It is still there.

Req 1b — MET. The replacement is marked "e.g." and hedged as "which happens to cover parentheses and two consecutive spaces too". Read cold, the synthetic path presents as an illustration of the character classes, not as the thing that was tested; the sentence that claims real testing points at real macOS session directories, which is what actually happened. No verification is asserted that did not occur. The honest structure survived the edit, which is what Req 1b was asking for.

Req 2 — MET, verified mechanically rather than by eye. Filtered the diff for any added or removed line that is not a comment: empty. Every changed line in scripts/launcher/ starts with //. Ran node scripts/launcher_test.js myself as the criterion requires: 59 tests, ALL LAUNCHER TESTS PASSED. See REPORTING ACCURACY below on the count.

Req 3 / 3a / 3b — MET, thoroughly. pipeman.md's new step 9 states that a release is two actions, that git push updates the repository and npm publish updates the registry, that npx fully-completely resolves from the registry and not from git, and that a release is not shipped until the registry serves the new version. Req 3a: scripts/verify-tarball.sh is named as the pre-publish check with the reason it is named there rather than left to the README. Req 3b: all three instances cited — 192de1d, 0fd7973, and sprint 3's own 89c8a74.
The step also adds a trigger nobody asked for and should have: "if a sprint's requirements bump package.json's version, treat that as the signal this step applies." A rule that tells you when it fires is worth more than one that waits to be remembered.
Renumbering checked: old step 9 became step 10, and no other file or section references pipeman's step numbers. That was the defect class I found in liveqa.md two sprints ago; it is not present here.

Req 4 — MET. package.json is 0.1.4 and the diff to that file is exactly one line.

Req 5 — MET. Ran scripts/verify-tarball.sh myself rather than reading the previous round's result. TARBALL VERIFICATION PASSED. In the installed target: docs/sprints/ holds only the seven .gitkeep placeholders, no registry.json, no state/*.json, no sprint markdown, no .claude/settings.local.json. Version marker reads 0.1.4 and the packed package.json reads 0.1.4.
The load-bearing check, done directly rather than inferred from the script's summary line: grep for the client name across the whole temp tree — tarball, unpacked package, and installed target — returns nothing, and the target's session.js carries the scrubbed comment with the synthetic example. The disclosure does not ship.

Req 6 — MET. Cumulative diff from 733f9c0 is confined to scripts/launcher/session.js, .claude/agents/pipeman.md and package.json, plus docs/sprints/ bookkeeping isolated in e2014ff. No lifecycle script, template or CLAUDE.md changes.

CRITERION SCOPE — NOT A DEFECT, BUT THE CRITERION AS WRITTEN IS NOT SATISFIABLE

Req 1's acceptance criterion is: grep -rn "Licenseprofessor" scripts/ templates/ .claude/commands/ docs/ returns nothing. It does not. It returns four hits, and I confirmed them independently rather than taking the handoff's word for it:
  docs/sprints/state/sprint-1.json (2), docs/sprints/state/sprint-3.json (3),
  docs/sprints/3-done/sprint-3_...--done.md (1), and sprint 4's own file (2).
Repo-wide grep outside .git finds nothing else. Nothing under scripts/, templates/ or .claude/commands/.

I am passing this, and the reasoning is not "close enough." Every one of those four is the audit trail quoting the finding, and clearing them would require breaking rules that outrank the criterion: CLAUDE.md forbids hand-editing anything under docs/sprints/state/, sprint 3's done-file is a closed historical record, and sprint 4's Context section is the sprint's own description of the bug it exists to fix — scrubbing it would leave a sprint file that cannot explain itself. None of the four ships; docs/sprints/ content is excluded from the tarball and I re-verified that this round rather than citing sprint 3's result.

So the criterion overshot the requirement it was testing. Req 1 is scoped to scripts/launcher/session.js; the criterion's grep is scoped to four directories including the entire audit trail, which makes it a criterion no role can clear without violating CLAUDE.md. That is the transition-precondition rule's own failure mode, in an acceptance criterion instead of a phase transition: a gate with no path through it. Master Controller should narrow the grep scope to the shipped surface for future sprints. Recorded here so the discrepancy is on the record rather than resolved silently.

Dev Team flagged this in the handoff and in the commit message before I looked, with the reasoning laid out. That is the correct move, and it is why this reads as a criterion-scope note rather than a finding.

REPORTING ACCURACY — NO VERDICT IMPACT, RECORDED BECAUSE IT KEEPS HAPPENING

The handoff and the commit message both claim node scripts/launcher_test.js passes "18/18". It passes 59/59. I counted the OK lines, and grepped the full output for the string "18" — zero occurrences anywhere. The substantive claim (passes unchanged, no behaviour change) is true and I verified it; the number attached to it is not from this suite.

This is the fourth count in four sprints that did not survive checking: 59 claimed when it was 58, 60 claimed when it was 59, and now 18 claimed when it is 59. It has never once been the code that was wrong. It is always the report describing the code. That is the exact through-line this epic was built around — sprint 2's defects were all the reporting layer disagreeing with actual state, and sprint 4's own pipeman.md addition exists because a state machine and a changelog both said a release had shipped when it had not.

No verdict impact: the artifact is correct and the requirement is met. But a handoff number that nobody generated is indistinguishable from one that is wrong in a direction that matters, and the only reason this one is harmless is that I ran the suite instead of believing it.

INFORMATIONAL — NOT THIS SPRINT

1. The scrubbed comment leaves a ragged short line ("// and single/double underscores —") where the reflow landed. Purely cosmetic, no reason to touch it inside a release sprint bounded by Req 6.

2. The same comment still says Windows "remains unverified until this sprint's Windows gate runs (see Risks in the sprint file)". That reference dangles: "this sprint" was sprint 1, now closed in 3-done, and a reader of session.js has no way to find it. Pre-existing, out of scope under Req 6, worth folding into the disclosure sweep already noted as follow-up in the sprint file.

3. For Pipeman, carried forward: npm pack packs the working tree, not the audited commit, and .vscode/settings.json is still dirty by design. Verified inert again this round — verify-tarball.sh's install produced a clean target.

4. For Pipeman, the point of Req 3: this sprint is not shipped when the push lands. Run scripts/verify-tarball.sh, then npm publish, then confirm the registry serves 0.1.4. The instruction now lives in your own file at step 9.

CODE QUALITY

Test coverage: none added, correctly — a comment edit, a doc edit, and a version string. Existing suite run and passing at 59.
Error handling: n/a, no executable line changed.
Standards compliance: comment-only diff proven mechanically; renumbering done without leaving a stale cross-reference; content and bookkeeping split into separate commits for the third sprint running.
Security: the disclosure this sprint exists to fix is gone from the shipped surface, verified in the installed target and not only in the source.

RECOMMENDATION

Ship it. /sprint-dev-done 4, then Pipeman ships 976f3d2 — and publishes. The scrub only reaches anyone once the registry serves 0.1.4.

PASS: PASS — round 1. Live-tested published npm 0.1.4, no browser (the package is the product). Environment: macOS, npx against the real registry, scratch dirs /tmp/fc4-upgrade (0.1.3 -> 0.1.4 upgrade) and /tmp/fc4-fresh (fresh install), 2026-08-29.

Nothing below is accepted from Pipeman's handoff. I re-ran the registry and client-name checks myself against the live registry rather than trusting the report, and the before/after evidence is my own.

CRITERION 1 — 0.1.4 ACTUALLY ON THE REGISTRY: PASS
`npm view fully-completely version` -> 0.1.4. dist-tags latest -> 0.1.4. `npm view fully-completely@0.1.4 gitHead` -> 976f3d2d594506e359eff0c34a592b9431d855b3, an exact match for last_shipped_commit, so the artifact I tested is provably the audited commit. This criterion existed because sprint 3 reached its live gate with nothing published; that is not the case here — the registry serves it.

CRITERION 2 — REAL 0.1.3 -> 0.1.4 UPGRADE: PASS
Installed 0.1.3 into /tmp/fc4-upgrade (marker 0.1.3), then upgraded. Printed verbatim: "Fully Completely: installed into /private/tmp/fc4-upgrade" / "Upgraded 0.1.3 -> 0.1.4". Asserted on the printed output as the criterion requires; the marker moving to 0.1.4 is corroboration, not the check. Replaced exactly one framework file: "scripts/launcher/session.js (upgraded, previous version backed up to scripts/launcher/session.js.fc-bak-0.1.3)".

No data loss. Before upgrading I planted realistic downstream data — a registry naming the target's OWN sprint, docs/sprints/state/sprint-1.json, a sprint markdown file, and a sentinel line appended to CLAUDE.md. All four verified intact by content afterwards (S4-STATE-MUST-SURVIVE, S4-SPRINT-MD-MUST-SURVIVE, "Downstream client sprint", S4-CLAUDEMD-MUST-SURVIVE). None of this repo's own sprint titles appear anywhere in the target.

CRITERION 3 — THE LOAD-BEARING GREP: PASS
Established the before-state rather than assuming it: the 0.1.3 target carried the client name at scripts/launcher/session.js:67, verbatim "// (`~/Programming/Licenseprofessor Edits and fixes`, seven such". After upgrade, that file contains ZERO occurrences. Checksum moved 7ef3299b... -> 6f21f6c5.... The scrub demonstrably reaches an existing install, which is the thing the sprint file said would be failing quietly if it did not. The machine-specific directory count ("seven such directories on this machine alone") is gone with it.

Fresh 0.1.4 install into /tmp/fc4-fresh: printed "Installed 0.1.4 (first install)"; a recursive grep of the entire target for the client name returns nothing at all. New installs are wholly clean.

CRITERION 4 — COMMENT SURVIVED THE SCRUB: PASS
I captured the full original comment block from the 0.1.3 target before upgrading, then read the shipped 0.1.4 version against it. All three elements Req 1a protects are intact in the shipped copy:
 - derived empirically — "This was verified by hand against real macOS session directories while building this";
 - re-verified across multiple character classes — "Re-verified against a path containing a space, two consecutive spaces, a dot, parentheses, and single/double underscores";
 - Windows flagged as extrapolation — "is the reasonable extrapolation, but Windows itself remains unverified until this sprint's Windows gate runs".
The replacement example is clearly synthetic: `~/Projects/Example Corp. (Staging)  Notes`. This is a scrub, not a trim.

I also checked the synthetic example against reality rather than taking it on its word. Running the shipped module: sessionsDir('/Users/x/Projects/Example Corp. (Staging)  Notes') -> '-Users-x-Projects-Example-Corp---Staging---Notes'. The space, dot, parentheses and two consecutive spaces each map to their own dash with no collapsing, exactly as the comment claims. The example is accurate, not decorative.

CRITERION 5 — NO SPRINT DATA IN TARGET: PASS
Fresh target's docs/sprints/ holds exactly the seven .gitkeep placeholders, 0 non-.gitkeep files. A find across the whole target for registry.json, sprint-N.json, sprint-N.md and settings.local.json returns nothing. Verified independently of QA1's tarball check.

REQ 2 SANITY, LIVE — no behaviour change survived into the shipped copy. Required the upgraded target's session.js in node: all six exports present (sessionId, sessionsDir, sessionFilePath, highestExistingGeneration, resolveSession, MAX_GENERATIONS); sessionId is deterministic for identical inputs, differs across generations, and matches the RFC UUIDv5 shape (version nibble 5, variant 8-b). The comment edit did not disturb the code it documents.

ISSUE 1 — MEDIUM, NOT A CRITERION FAILURE, NEEDS A SCOPE RULING BEFORE ANYONE CALLS THE SCRUB COMPLETE

The upgrade removes the client name from session.js and simultaneously writes it back to disk in the same directory, under a different name. install.js backs the old file up before replacing it, so the upgraded target contains:

  scripts/launcher/session.js.fc-bak-0.1.3:67:// (`~/Programming/Licenseprofessor Edits and fixes`, seven such

Confirmed live in /tmp/fc4-upgrade after a real 0.1.3 -> 0.1.4 upgrade.

Why this is not a FAIL or CONDITIONAL from me. Every one of my five criteria is met on its own terms — criterion 3 is scoped to scripts/launcher/session.js in the installed project, and that file is clean. The backup is deliberate, pre-existing install.js design that protects a user's local modifications, and it is announced in plain text in the installer's own printed output rather than happening silently. Net exposure inside a user's own project is unchanged by this release: the string was already on their disk in session.js before the upgrade and is on their disk in the backup after it. This release does not make anything worse, and for fresh installs — the majority path from here — it makes it perfect.

Why it still matters. The sprint's objective is information-disclosure remediation, and on the upgrade path the remediation is incomplete: a user who upgrades specifically to get the scrub still has the client name in their working tree. I checked whether it propagates and it can — the target's .gitignore, written by install.js itself, contains only "docs/sprints/.locks/" and does NOT cover *.fc-bak-*. A downstream project running `git add -A` after upgrading commits the client name into its own repository history. That is a plausible path from "already public on npm" to "in an unrelated client's git history."

This is a live-only finding by construction. No static audit could surface it: the backup file does not exist in the tarball, does not exist in the diff, and does not exist until a real upgrade runs. QA1's Req 5 tarball check was correct and would never have seen it.

Suggested home, not my call: a follow-up sprint adding *.fc-bak-* to the .gitignore block install.js writes, and/or a line in the installer's output noting that a backup may retain content the release removed. That is Master Controller's scope decision, the same way the original session.js item was in sprint 3.

ISSUE 2 — LOW, INFORMATIONAL. The Windows illustration in the shipped comment still reads `C:\Users\Chris Hobbs\...`. I checked this deliberately and am NOT raising it as a disclosure: that is the package author's own name, already published intentionally in package.json's "author" field, and Req 1 is scoped to the client project name and the machine directory count, both of which are gone. Recorded only so the next reader does not re-open it as a missed scrub.

ISSUE 3 — LOW, INFORMATIONAL, QA1'S CALL ALREADY MADE. Req 1b asks that the synthetic example not be presented as the thing that was tested. The shipped sentence reads "a real repo path containing a space or a dot (e.g. `~/Projects/Example Corp. (Staging)  Notes`, ...)", which places a synthetic path inside a clause about a real one. "e.g." signals illustration and I read it as acceptable; QA1 audited Req 1b directly and passed it. Noted for completeness, not as a dispute.

WHAT I OBSERVED VS ACCEPTED
Everything above I ran and observed directly on macOS against the live npm registry. No component of this sprint's criteria requires Windows or any other party, so unlike sprint 1 there is nothing accepted on report.

RECOMMENDATION
Ship-ready. All five LiveQA criteria pass with evidence, and the sprint's central claim — that a framework-owned scrub propagates to existing installs on upgrade — is proven by a real before/after rather than inferred from ownership rules. The backup-file residue in Issue 1 is the one thing that should be decided before anyone describes the client name as fully scrubbed from installed projects; it does not block this release. This PASS means the code is ready, not that anyone is authorized to close sprint 4.
